items.title: Recursive launches Flint, a free 40B MoE coding model that runs on laptops
items.summary: Recursive (Richard Socher's startup) released Flint, a 40B mixture-of-experts model with only 2.5B active parameters, under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face. It reaches about 131 tokens/s on a MacBook Pro M4 Pro and beats other sub-50B models on SWE-Bench Verified. The company says it was largely built by its own AI research system.
items.whyItMatters: A tiny-active-parameter MoE running fast locally shows where cheap on-device inference for tutor tooling and dev workflows is heading, though it is a coding model rather than a voice one.

items.title: Meta says its Muse AI agent has passed 10M users, with shopping a top use
items.summary: About 25% of Muse users are active daily, and shopping and personal productivity (email, calendar) lead usage. Meta plans a free tier with commerce commissions plus a paid premium tier, and says it expects over 10x compute-efficiency gains within a year.
items.whyItMatters: Shows how a big consumer AI assistant plans to monetize (free tier plus commissions, paid premium models), which is a useful reference for pricing a tutor.
